title: Filtered-injective representatives and Hom computation in the filtered localization
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives [def-sp-abelian, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Write $\operatorname{Fil}^f(\mathcal A)$ for objects with a finite decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration], and let $K_F^+(\mathcal A)$ be the homotopy category of bounded-below cochain complexes of these objects. Morphisms and chain homotopies preserve every filtration step; the graded complexes are the quotients $\operatorname{gr}^pK=F^pK/F^{p+1}K$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Let $DF^+(\mathcal A)$ be its localization at chain maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on all graded complexes. A filtered object is called filtered injective if all its graded objects are injective in $\mathcal A$; write $\mathcal I^f$ for their full additive subcategory. Every $K\in K_F^+(\mathcal A)$ admits a filtered quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ with $I$ bounded below and termwise filtered injective. For every such $I$ and every bounded-below filtered complex $K$, localization induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{K_F^+(\mathcal A)}(K,I)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{DF^+(\mathcal A)}(K,I).$$
The canonical functor $K^+(\mathcal I^f)\to DF^+(\mathcal A)$ is an exact equivalence of triangulated categories. Forgetting the filtration and every $\operatorname{gr}^p$ send these representatives to bounded-below complexes of ordinary injectives and commute with the equivalence and the canonical functors to $D^+(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All the assertions restrict to any fixed finite filtration interval $[a,b]$, meaning $F^aK=K$ and $F^{b+1}K=0$, with resolutions in that same interval.

proof.text: Use the filtration and quotient conventions of [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Kernels have the induced subobject filtration; cokernels and coimages have the quotient filtration. A strict short exact sequence means an underlying short exact sequence whose maps are strict; its graded sequences are short exact, by the formulas for the induced and quotient filtrations. Conversely graded exact sequences are strict exact by [lem-trf-finite-filtered-graded-exactness]. Filtered cone triangles and their localization are supplied by [lem-trf-filtered-cone-localization]. Shifting the cochain index lets us assume $K^n=0$ for $n<0$.

source.place: Tags 05RX and 05TW, exact-category conventions and shift reduction

proof.text: First resolve a single finite filtered object $X$. By [lem-trf-enough-strict-filtered-injectives] choose a strict monomorphism $X\to J^0$, put $Q^0=\operatorname{coker}(X\to J^0)$ with its quotient filtration, choose a strict monomorphism $Q^0\to J^1$, and repeat with $Q^{r+1}=\operatorname{coker}(Q^r\to J^{r+1})$. Define $d_J^r$ by $J^r\twoheadrightarrow Q^r\hookrightarrow J^{r+1}$. Its square is zero. Each augmented graded sequence is exact by the strict quotient formulas of Step 1. Thus $X[0]\to J$ is a filtered quasi-isomorphism, $J^{<0}=0$, all $J^r$ are filtered injective, and the augmented differentials are strict. This construction uses enough injectives only through the cited strict-embedding result.

For a map $f:X\to Y$ and two resolutions as in Step 2, lift it to a chain map $f^r:J_X^r\to J_Y^r$. Extend $X\to Y\to J_Y^0$ across the strict monomorphism $X\to J_X^0$ using [lem-trf-enough-strict-filtered-injectives]. Once $f^r$ is chosen, $d_Y^rf^r$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}d_X^{r-1}$, hence factors through $\operatorname{coker}d_X^{r-1}=\operatorname{im}d_X^r$. This equality, with its induced filtration, follows from [lem-trf-finite-filtered-graded-exactness] applied to the augmented resolution. Extend this factor across the strict inclusion $\operatorname{im}d_X^r\hookrightarrow J_X^{r+1}$ into the filtered injective $J_Y^{r+1}$. This defines $f^{r+1}$ and gives $f^{r+1}d_X^r=d_Y^rf^r$.

For a strict exact sequence $0\to X\xrightarrow{i}Y\xrightarrow{\pi}Z\to0$, resolve $X,Z$ by $J,H$. Extend $X\to J^0$ to $b:Y\to J^0$ using [lem-trf-enough-strict-filtered-injectives]. The map $d_Jb$ factors through $\pi$, defining $t:Z\to J^1$. Extend $-t$ across $Z\hookrightarrow H^0$ to $c^0:H^0\to J^1$. Inductively, $d_Jc^r$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}d_H^{r-1}$: for $r=0$ this is the augmented $Z$, and subsequently it follows from the previous identity $d_Jc^{r-1}+c^rd_H^{r-1}=0$. By strict exactness [lem-trf-finite-filtered-graded-exactness], factor through $\operatorname{im}d_H^r$ and extend its negative to $c^{r+1}:H^{r+1}\to J^{r+2}$. Set $M^r=J^r\oplus H^r$ and $d_M=\begin{pmatrix}d_J&c\\0&d_H\end{pmatrix}$. The identity just imposed gives $d_M^2=0$, and $(b,(Z\to H^0)\pi)$ is an augmentation $Y[0]\to M$. This yields a termwise split sequence $0\to J\to M\to H\to0$. After each graded functor, the natural long exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact, lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] show that this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, since the outside augmentations are so: in nonzero degrees all outside cohomology vanishes, and in degree zero the short exact sequences identify the middle map as an isomorphism. Finite sums of injectives are injective by extending each component separately, so every $M^r$ is filtered injective.

Put $Z_i=\ker d_K^i$ and $B_i=\operatorname{coim}d_K^i$, with the filtrations from Step 1. The sequence $0\to Z_i\to K^i\to B_i\to0$ is strict exact directly from its subobject and quotient filtrations. Resolve $Z_i,B_i$ by $J_i,H_i$ using Step 2. Lift $u_i:B_i\to Z_{i+1}$ to $\widetilde u_i:H_i\to J_{i+1}$ using Step 3, and use Step 4 to obtain $0\to J_i\xrightarrow{\alpha_i}M_i\xrightarrow{\beta_i}H_i\to0$ with compatible augmentation of $K^i[0]$. The horizontal differential $\partial_i=\alpha_{i+1}\widetilde u_i\beta_i$ satisfies $\partial_{i+1}\partial_i=0$ because $\beta_{i+1}\alpha_{i+1}=0$; it commutes with the resolution differentials because all three factors are chain maps. Its augmentation is $d_K^i$, by the lifting and augmentation equations. We have therefore constructed the first-quadrant double complex $D^{i,r}=M_i^r$ and an augmentation $K\to D$ supported in resolution degree zero [def-sp-double-complex-total].

Take $I^n=\bigoplus_{i+r=n}D^{i,r}$ with differential $\partial+(-1)^i d_{M_i}$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Each sum is finite, hence is a finite filtered object with injective graded pieces; $I^{<0}=0$. The degree-$n$ augmentation is $K^n\to D^{n,0}\hookrightarrow I^n$. For each filtration index $p$, the additive functor $\operatorname{gr}^p$ commutes with these finite sums and differentials. Every resolution column $\operatorname{gr}^p K^i[0]\to\operatorname{gr}^p M_i$ is a quasi-isomorphism by Step 4. Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation], with the resolution index first, namely the flipped bicomplex $D^{\prime\,r,i}=D^{i,r}$. The two total complexes are identified by multiplication by $(-1)^{ir}$ on the $(i,r)$ summand: a horizontal differential changes that sign by $(-1)^r$ and a vertical differential by $(-1)^i$, which identifies $\partial+(-1)^i d_{M_i}$ with $d_{M_i}+(-1)^r\partial$. The sign is $1$ on the resolution-zero augmentation. Its augmentation hypotheses are exactly the chain-map and vanishing equations of Step 5. It gives $\operatorname{gr}^pK\to\operatorname{gr}^pI$ a quasi-isomorphism. Shift back to the original lower bound. This proves existence of the required representative.

proof.text: Let $A$ be graded acyclic and $I$ bounded below and termwise filtered injective. For a filtered chain map $f:A\to I$, construct a filtered homotopy $h^n:A^n\to I^{n-1}$. Start with $h^n=0$ below the lower bound $N$ of $I$. Having $h^n$ and the identities in smaller degrees, set $r^n=f^n-d_I^{n-1}h^n$. The chain-map equation and the previous identity give $r^nd_A^{n-1}=0$. By [lem-trf-finite-filtered-graded-exactness], the acyclic graded sequences imply strict exactness of $A$, so $r^n$ factors through $A^n/\operatorname{im}d_A^{n-1}=\operatorname{im}d_A^n$ with its induced filtration. Extend that factor across the strict inclusion $\operatorname{im}d_A^n\hookrightarrow A^{n+1}$ into $I^n$ using [lem-trf-enough-strict-filtered-injectives], and call it $h^{n+1}$. Then $f^n=d_I^{n-1}h^n+h^{n+1}d_A^n$. Induction gives the homotopy in every degree, also when $A$ has no lower bound. Thus all maps from a graded acyclic complex to $I$ are nullhomotopic.

For a filtered quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to L$, its cone and shifted cone are graded acyclic by [lem-trf-filtered-cone-localization]. Precomposition $s^*:\operatorname{Hom}(L,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,I)$ in the homotopy category is bijective, as follows directly from Step 7 and the cone formulas [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For surjectivity, a chain map $a:K\to I$ composed with $C(s)[-1]\to K$ has a nullhomotopy whose components are $(b^{n-1},h^n):L^{n-1}\oplus K^n\to I^{n-1}$. The homotopy equation on the first summand says $b:L\to I$ is a chain map; on the second it says $a=d_Ih+hd_K-bs$. Hence $a$ is homotopic to $(-b)s$. For injectivity, if $bs=d_Ih+hd_K$, the components $(b^n,h^{n+1})$ define a map $C(s)\to I$: substituting the cone differential verifies the chain-map equation. Step 7 makes it nullhomotopic, and restriction along $L\to C(s)$ makes $b$ nullhomotopic.

Write $\mathcal K=K_F^+(\mathcal A)$ and $Q:\mathcal K\to DF^+(\mathcal A)$. By Step 8 the contravariant functor $H=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal K}(-,I)$ inverts every filtered quasi-isomorphism, so it descends through localization to $\overline H$. The maps $H(X)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{DF^+}(QX,QI)$ induced by $Q$ are natural for ordinary arrows and, because both functors invert denominators, for their inverses and every localized composite. For a localized arrow $v:QX\to QI$, define $\rho(v)=\overline H(v)(1_I)$. Naturality gives $\rho(Qf)=f$ and $Q\rho(v)=v$, by applying that naturality to $v$ and $1_I$. Thus $Q$ gives the asserted Hom bijection. This universal-property argument supplies both injectivity and surjectivity without assuming a fraction calculus for the filtered category.

The canonical functor $K^+(\mathcal I^f)\to DF^+(\mathcal A)$ is essentially surjective by Step 6 and fully faithful by Step 9. Filtered injectives are closed under finite sums (extend components separately), shifts and cone terms; their homotopy category has the cone triangulation. By [lem-trf-filtered-cone-localization] its inclusion followed by localization preserves precisely these cone triangles, hence is exact. Full faithfulness and essential surjectivity give the asserted exact equivalence.

For a finite filtered injective object $J$, descend through the finite filtration: the highest nonzero $F^pJ=\operatorname{gr}^pJ$ is injective; if $F^{p+1}J$ is injective then its inclusion in $F^pJ$ splits by extending its identity [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Thus $F^pJ\cong F^{p+1}J\oplus\operatorname{gr}^pJ$ is injective, since its two components extend separately. This proves the underlying object is injective; every graded object is injective by definition. The forgetting functor sends graded acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes, by applying [lem-trf-finite-filtered-graded-exactness] in each degree; hence it sends filtered quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms by taking their cones [lem-trf-filtered-cone-localization]. Each graded functor does so by definition. The two squares now commute before localization termwise, and after localization by its universal property. This proves all comparisons with $D^+(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: Fix $a\le b$. The same-interval clause of [lem-trf-enough-strict-filtered-injectives] keeps each embedding of Step 2 in $[a,b]$; quotients retain these bounds, so all single-object resolutions do too. Kernels, coimages and images in Steps 3–5 inherit these same bounds from their subobject or quotient filtrations [def-sp-filtration]. In Step 4 the terms $J^r\oplus H^r$ retain the bounds and the extended maps preserve every filtration step. The finite diagonal sums in Step 6 retain the bounds. Step 7 constructs only filtered maps between the given objects; its extension property changes no object and hence no interval. Steps 8–9 apply inside this bounded-interval category, where cones, shifts and localization have the structure in [lem-trf-filtered-cone-localization]. Steps 10–11 then give the restricted exact equivalence and the same forgetting and graded squares. For $a=b$ these constructions are ordinary injective resolutions placed in that one filtration degree; for the zero complex one may choose zero throughout.

split_report.summary: Second reading repaired the definitions-only proof: strict filtered injectivity and graded exactness are stated as smaller dependencies, filtered cone localization is supplied independently of injectives, and the object resolution, comparison lifts, horseshoe, double-complex augmentation, contraction and cone Hom computation are written out. Reuses the existing first-quadrant augmentation theorem; no clause of the item is repackaged as a new node.

tool_uses.why: Generic first-quadrant augmented-column totalization comparison in any abelian category. The trace-formula route has no such algebra lemma; applied only after each graded functor, with no sheaf or Grothendieck hypothesis.
